title: The Ground Beneath Your Feet Is Moving
hook: What if your compass pointed south instead of north?
script: What if your compass pointed south instead of north? Earth's magnetic poles have swapped places hundreds of times, often without warning. The last full flip was about 780,000 years ago during the Brunhes-Matuyama reversal. This phenomenon occurs due to molten iron moving in the Earth's outer core. During the last reversal, Earth's magnetic field strength dropped to just 10% of today's level. Amazingly, these flips take thousands of years, creating a gradual shift rather than a sudden change. The record of these flips is frozen into the rock of the ocean floor like a barcode written by the planet itself. So the ground beneath your feet is far less permanent than it feels.
